findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple live nymphs along the wall of the back storage room, between the soda boxes and standing coolers. Multiple dead and live roaches (in various sages of development) were observed on glue traps today. A dead roach was also observed directly beneath the soda lid holders (in an area the inspector noted was in need of cleaning during the last inspection).
Glue traps have either NOT been date marked, or not REPLACED since the last follow up inspection. Today is the third follow up inspection since 09/15 original inspection, and the proliferation of roaches has gotten worse. 
Roach sightings are being logged in a blue Steritech binder, however only two sightings have been noted since the last follow up. The facility has increased the frequency at which pest control services the establishment to biweekly, however the presence of nymphs indicates that the adults are breeding.
Facility must coordinate cleaning efforts with maintenance (to fill and seal holes/ gaps which may be harboring roaches), as well as their pest control operator to ensure the elimination and of harborage conditions, and to stop the proliferation of roaches.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple dead roaches on insect traps, as well as in the under-counter cabinetry. Live roaches were also observed on the traps, from adult to larval stages. Employees are currently logging pest sightings in a blue “Steritech” binder. Nine roach sightings have been reported during the past month in the binder in areas including the bar, near the water heater, in the manager office, as well as in areas where ready-to-eat food is held. On 10/07/25 the pest control technician noted that the areas in the pest log had been chemically treated, and gel bait was applied.

 If dead roaches are spotted they should be immediately removed, and the area they were in should be cleaned. Remove all conditions for harborage, including spilt food and beverages, as well as cardboard. Write the date on glue traps to better monitor pests. The frequency at which pest control is providing services to the facility is currently inadequate. Increase services to biweekly treatments. The inspector will return on 10/29/25 to check pest control management. Ensure the facility has proof of service available as well as a minimum six month contract with a pest control provider to show during the follow up inspection.

findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employee at concession stand was observed sweeping and emptying the dust pan prior to putting on gloves to check the temperature of hotdogs on the roller grill. Handwashing did not occur between tasks. Proper handwashing was discussed, and employee was observed washing hands as needed between tasks for remainder of inspection. 
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed before putting on gloves and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Paper towels were used to shut off the manual faucet prior to drying hands. Proper technique was discussed. Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. Once paper towels are used to shut off the faucet they are contaminated. Get new paper towels to finish drying hands if additional drying is needed.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

Maintain quat solutions at 200-400ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) PIC was unfamiliar with employee health policy requirements. PIC described the process for cleaning up should someone become ill in the lobby and did not mention a step for disinfection. PIC noted a body fluid cleanup kit is available through the company to be used on-site and might have a disinfecting product that comes with it, but a kit was not present at the time of inspection. Several old food handler certifications were available for employees that no longer work at the facility, and only one of the current employees has a valid food handler certification. Priority violations for handwashing were also observed. Violations will be revisited at the follow-up inspection on 10/14/21. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed copies of employee health reporting agreements were not available for the PIC and other employees at the time of inspection. PIC signed a copy for himself and began to have employees review and sign copies as available during inspection. The presence of signed reporting agreements for all staff will be verified at the follow-up inspection on 10/14/21. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 PIC was unfamiliar with what products were available for disinfection during cleanup after a vomit/diarrhea event. PIC described the process for cleaning up should someone become ill in the lobby and did not mention a step for disinfection. PIC noted a body fluid cleanup kit is available through the company to be used on-site and might have a disinfecting product that comes with it, but a kit was not present at the time of inspection. In the meantime, a copy of norovirus disinfection policy was provided. Maxim Lemon Detergent Disinfectant (used to inhibit mildew on carpeting/seats) is available for use if needed and is a virucide to norovirus. PIC stated he would look into company policies to find out more information.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed

Cleaning product intended to aid in unclogging drains was used in an attempt to allow for proper drainage. After using a plunger black debris came up out of the drain. PIC indicated the sink in question is the one most frequently used for handwashing by staff. If multiple handwashes were needed in a row, the water would not drain properly and would create a potential situation where dirty water was filling the basin and splashing back up on hands. PIC was advised to submit a work order for proper repairs. Limit use of said handwashing sink until it is draining properly and have staff use the front handwashing sink in the food service area more frequently for the time being. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times.

findings.citation_text:
4-501.14 Upper edges and seams of 3 part sink basins and faucet handles were soiled with grease buildup. Clean the 3 part sink and faucets daily/as needed. Ensure removal of gross debris accumulation prior to ware washing. 
The compartments of sinks, basins, or other receptacles used for washing and rinsing equipment and utensils shall be cleaned: (A) before use, (B) throughout the day at a frequency necessary to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils and to ensure that the equipment performs its intended function; and (C) if used, at least every 24 hours.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Liquid waste was puddling in the bottom of the holder for the left beverage gun at the bar. Liquid waste was not draining properly, and a half dozen fruit flies were observed in the area due to the presence of the liquid waste. The drain hose was disconnected to remove liquid waste from the holder. GM was advised to have facilities manager work with beverage distributor to resolve the drainage issue. Ensure liquid waste is removed nightly and all surfaces are cleaned and sanitized.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Handsinks and related fixtures in front food service area and in back ware washing area were soiled with greasy/grimy buildup. Clean handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed, and maintain them clean. 
--Drains behind beverage machines where Freestyle and Icee drain lines empty were soiled with mold buildup. Clean the drains and the drain lines that empty into the drains as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. 
--Floor drain under Freestyle machine on the north end of the food service area was heavily soiled with buildup of popping corn kernels and debris. Clean the floor drain.
--Electrical conduit bracket behind the Freestyle machine on the north end of the food service counter was observed with an accumulation of popping corn kernels. Clean the bracket.
--Floor in downstairs dry good storage room was observed with an accumulation of spilled popping corn kernels under bulk storage area. Clean the floor under bulk popping corn storage. 
--Floor in back storage area under ice machines and other equipment was soiled with general debris accumulation. Clean the floor in the back storage area. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to prepare a food order. Proper handwashing and glove use were discussed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.650 - Plastic ice scoop was observed to be cracked. Replace the damaged ice scoop.

One of the screws on the metal ice sensor hanging down in the ice machine is rusty. Rust is beginning to run down the sensor. Replace the rusty screw in the ice machine.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1120 - Handsinks were observed to be soiled with buildup. Front handsink had grease and dust accumulation, while the back handsink had a general buildup of grime. Sink up front was cleaned during the inspection.

Clean handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed, and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1220 - Floor under ice machines and equipment in back was soiled food debris and general buildup. Clean the floors under the equipment in the back storage area.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1320 - Sanitizer concentration was +400ppm quat in the spray bottle at the front counter. Solution was dispensing too strong from the wall mounted chemical dispenser at the 3 part sink. A smaller dispensing tip was placed in the hose and brought the concentration down, but it still appeared to be stronger than 200ppm. Per instructions for chemical being used the concentration is to be 200ppm. A call for service was made to have a technician come out for service to check all components and make any necessary repairs.
NOTE: Use test strips and verify the concentration is at 200ppm. Dilute solutions slightly with water if the sanitizer is stronger than 200ppm.

Chemicals must not be used in any manner that poses a potential risk of cross contamination nor in any manner that may pose a hazard to persons exposed to and/or using the chemicals.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 1160: Observed droppings in the rightside of the cabinets. Clean droppings and sanitize the surrounding area.
